identity.operation: Parse more than five AAAA answers and write their TTL entries.
identity.condition: A packet contains at least six valid AAAA answers, while the entry supplies a five-element IPv6 TTL array and count 5.
identity.capability: The AAAA parser call must provide capacity for more than five TTL entries.
identity.consequence: The sixth AAAA TTL write cannot be exercised.

requirement: Reach AAAA parsing with capacity for more than five returned address TTL entries.

assessment.necessity_reason: The parser writes a TTL entry when its address index is below caller capacity, and the harness fixes that capacity at five. The supplied delegated parser calls an unread append helper for matching AAAA records, so the packet does not establish that a six-answer input can produce a sixth address node.

before.requirement: For a packet yielding at least six AAAA address nodes, provide capacity to write the sixth IPv6 TTL entry.
before.reason: The visible capacity check would permit a sixth write with a larger caller array, while the old harness supplies five slots. Whether six valid answers can reach that check depends on the unread node helpers.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The delegated answer loop calls the unread node append helper for each matching AAAA record.
The delegated parser calls the unread concatenation helper before the AAAA parser counts address nodes.

after.requirement: For a packet yielding at least six AAAA address nodes, provide capacity to write the sixth IPv6 TTL entry.
after.reason: The capacity check remains present and the old harness still supplies five slots. The unread node helpers and build integration prevent a certain after-side reachability assessment.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The delegated answer loop calls the unread node append helper for each matching AAAA record.
The delegated parser calls the unread concatenation helper before the AAAA parser counts address nodes.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The complete entry shows no other call sequence that supplies more IPv6 TTL slots.
The target uses the autotools build and links the resulting static library.

assessment.comparison_reason: The five-slot caller constraint is identical for both source versions. Whether it blocks a required sixth AAAA TTL write remains unproved on either side.
missing_information: Read both versions of ares__append_addrinfo_node and ares__addrinfo_cat_nodes to establish six-node reachability.

necessity_evidence.reason: The AAAA parser permits TTL output beyond five entries when caller capacity is larger, while the old harness always supplies five slots. The packet does not establish that six valid AAAA answers can produce six address nodes under the supplied build.

scope_contract.reason: AAAA reply parsing and its caller-sized IPv6 TTL output are part of this entry's operational surface.

feasible_trigger.reason: The answer loop calls an unread node append helper, and an unread concatenation helper supplies the nodes counted by the AAAA parser. The supplied new source list also does not establish its integration into the autotools build.

evidence.dependency_reason: The loop calls the unread append helper for matching AAAA answers.
The unread concatenation helper transfers parsed nodes to the AAAA parser.
The new source list names the AAAA parser; its inclusion by the autotools recipe is not shown.

observable_consequence.reason: Conditional on six IPv6 address nodes, the fixed count of five prevents the sixth TTL entry from being written, although the parser counts all IPv6 addresses.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete entry has one AAAA parser call, always with five TTL slots. Its possible sixth host address is a different output and does not write the sixth IPv6 TTL entry.

identity_preserved.reason: The same AAAA TTL capacity condition and the same old harness apply on both sides. The supplied g0118 source-list addition does not itself establish a new parser contract.

evidence.dependency_reason: g0118 names the parser in the new source list.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: Write the sixth IPv6 TTL entry for a valid reply yielding six matching AAAA address nodes, if that node count is reachable.
coverage_witness.required_setup: An IPv6 TTL array with at least six elements and an input count of at least six.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: A five-element IPv6 TTL array and input count 5.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: The sixth IPv6 TTL write is skipped by the caller-capacity check.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: The complete entry has no second AAAA call or other route that supplies more than five IPv6 TTL slots.
